User request: No tools are available. In this JavaScript snippet, what does `source` mean? `const source = items.filter(Boolean);`

content.text:
"source" is just a variable name. The expression creates a new array containing only the truthy elements of items.

- items.filter(Boolean) calls Array.prototype.filter with the built-in Boolean function as the predicate. Boolean(x) coerces x to true/false.
- filter keeps elements for which the predicate returns true, so this removes all falsy values: false, 0, "", null, undefined, and NaN.
- const means the binding source can't be reassigned, but the array object it refers to can still be mutated.

Example:
- items = [0, 1, false, 2, "", 3, null]
- source = items.filter(Boolean) // => [1, 2, 3]
